claim: Methotrexate DHFR Ki = 1e-7 mM (0.1 nM), median of 3 ChEMBL activities
original_status: computed from ChEMBL, unverified against primary literature
finding: ChEMBL activities RE-CONFIRMED live: 3055901=0.077 nM (CHEMBL1152608, Bioorg Med Chem 2009), 939069=0.179 nM (CHEMBL1131724, Bioorg Med Chem Lett 1999, T. cruzi DHFR -- NOT human), 18251252=0.01 nM (CHEMBL4052640, Eur J Med Chem 2017). Median=0.077 nM -> BEES used 0.1 nM, close but not an exact median match (0.077 vs 0.1, ~30% off). IMPORTANT: activity 939069 is for Trypanosoma cruzi DHFR, not human DHFR -- the median composition is not species-pure. Separately, Volpato et al. 2009 (full text) explicitly states wild-type human DHFR Ki_MTX = 3.4 pM (0.0034 nM) -- ~23x tighter than the ChEMBL median and ~29x tighter than the BEES value.
action: Two issues to fix: (1) activity 939069 is T. cruzi DHFR, not human -- exclude it from the human-DHFR median, or re-pull a human-only ChEMBL activity set. (2) The literature (Volpato 2009) reports a much tighter Ki (3.4 pM = 3.4e-9 mM) than either the ChEMBL median or the value BEES used. Recommend replacing 1e-7 mM with 3.4e-9 mM sourced to Volpato et al. 2009 (PMID 19478082), or at minimum footnoting the ~23-30x discrepancy between ChEMBL assay-derived and kinetically-derived Ki.
